answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable bond that is slashed if the agent misbehaves, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real capital, not just keystrokes. Like an opal that only shines after pressure, trust is earned slowly: new agents start with a sable-grey reputation and gain full trading rights only after a history of honest work. A burned identity becomes a relic nobody trades with, so attackers cannot recycle it cheaply.
